result:
**Verdict: FAIL.** The repaired DG1 candidate (`sha256:991d3241…a8fc`, commit `f32c705`) still can't pass: the required browser end-to-end suite is red in Arabic, and one of my assigned findings (F-DG1-005) is only partly fixed.

I recomputed the candidate ID and it matches. The repository HEAD is `18c1e61`, which is `f32c705` plus the freeze commit; that commit only adds excluded metadata (assignments, manifest, `stages.json`). I ran everything in a throwaway clone at `f32c705` and deleted it afterwards. No product file was changed.

**Passed on this candidate:**
- **Install and static checks:** the offline frozen-lockfile install changed nothing (371 packages reused, 0 downloaded). Typecheck, build, lint, the OpenAPI lint (33 operations), the no-CDN scan and the colour-contrast check all pass.
- **Unit tests:** 210/210.
- **Integration tests:** 193/193 on two separate fresh PostgreSQL 16 databases, with no unhandled errors. The contract test now covers all 33 operations, including `getBrandingTokens`.
- **Database checks:** my own probe confirms migrations 0001–0008 apply to an empty database. The audit table rejects UPDATE and DELETE, even for the owner.
- **Acceptance suites:** A12 (cross-scope 404), A13 (job idempotency), A14 (409/428 concurrency) and A18 (clean start with a real install, /healthz and /readyz) pass. So do A20 (bilingual shell) and A20 token propagation, which changed a colour token in the copy and saw it rendered.
- **Gate validator:** the register, pipeline and reconcile checks all pass.

**Assigned findings:**

| Finding | Severity | Result |
|---|---|---|
| F-DG1-201 | High | PASS → closed. The contract suite now exercises `getBrandingTokens` and is green. |
| F-DG1-101 | High | PASS → closed. Its stale-evidence leftover is split out as F-DG1-209. |
| F-DG1-110 | Low | PASS → closed. The flaky tests are now scoped to their own request and close connections before the database drop; clean in both runs. |
| F-DG1-004 | Low | PASS → closed. In both English and Arabic, a Lead with a business-unit grant creates a record and reaches its detail page; a user with no grants gets 404. |
| F-DG1-005 | Low | **FAIL → stays open.** The transformation's own audit changes are now localized. But records created by such a Lead also show a new "assignment created" audit entry (added by the F-DG1-106 fix). In both languages it displays a raw action code, raw field names and raw IDs/JSON. |

The web edit form no longer offers "closed" (only draft/active, or active/on hold). A direct API request to close returns 422 and leaves the record unchanged. That finding belongs to the domain reviewer, so I recorded it as a check rather than closing it.

**New findings:**
- **F-DG1-208 (High, mandatory, owner frontend-ux-engineer):** the end-to-end suite fails deterministically (13 passed, 1 failed, 6 did not run; same result on a re-run). At `apps/web/e2e/journeys.spec.ts:138`, the test looks for the Arabic "My Work" link (عملي) with an unanchored pattern. The new Arabic "BAU and Improvement" label from the glossary fix `a5ff652` contains that same text, so the test matches two links and stops. The 6 remaining Arabic journeys (create, list, edit, archive, administration, no-roles user) never run. In the throwaway copy only, anchoring that one pattern gives 20/20, so the screens work and the defect is in the test. The frontend handback confirms these journeys weren't run before the freeze.
- **F-DG1-209 (Low, owner transformation-analyst):** REQ-S19-004 and REQ-DLV-033 still cite the 181-test integration log from before the repairs. The REQ-S19-004 note still says "migrations 0001-0006".

**Requirements:** all 12 are marked complete and every cited evidence file exists. REQ-DLV-033 isn't actually complete while its bilingual end-to-end evidence is red (F-DG1-208). REQ-S19-004 cites outdated evidence (F-DG1-209), though the behaviour itself is correct.

**Blocked or not covered:**
- `pnpm deps:verify` needs the package registry and there's no network here. It wasn't an assigned check.
- A live CI run where a failing gate stops the pipeline (A24, for REQ-DLV-025) can't be observed here.
- The screen a creator sees when they genuinely can't open their new record is covered only by unit tests.
- The local pnpm package store is read-only in this sandbox, so installs used a copy of it in scratch space.

I wrote two new test assets for later promotion into `tests/qa/`: a browser test for the web repairs and the database probe script.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG1/round-2/qa-verifier.json`
- `reviews/DG1/round-2/qa-verifier.findings.json`
- `reviews/DG1/round-2/qa-verifier.verifications.json`
- `reviews/DG1/round-2/qa-verifier.md`
- `test-evidence/DG1/qa/round-2/` (logs and EN/AR screenshots; index in `README.md`)
- `test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/dg1-r2-web-repairs.spec.ts`
- `test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/dg1-r2-schema-probe.sh`
